claim: Under Parakramabahu I, the Gal Vihara rock inscription records a formal programme regulating the Buddhist clergy, with a historical introduction followed by disciplinary injunctions; it is direct epigraphic evidence for a twelfth-century monastic reform and regulatory project.
bounded_by: The inscription establishes a normative reform programme, not complete compliance, uniformity of lived monastic practice or the neutrality of royal reform rhetoric.
notes: Promotes the defensible core of GF-SAS-09.
